content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in TypeScript: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `main.ts`. Build and run it with Deno — `deno run`, `deno check` and `deno test`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. --- total 16 drwxr-xr-x 4 vshynkarenko staff 128 11 Okt. 13:38 . drwxr-xr-x 3 vshynkarenko staff 96 11 Okt. 13:38 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1861 11 Okt. 13:38 BRIEF.md -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1279 13 Sep. 17:41 main.ts

content.text:
The four additions are in `main.ts`. It type-checks with `deno check`, and sample runs produce the output the brief specifies. The original `add`, `done` and `list` behave as before. **What changed** - **`prio

`**: each task now has a priority, defaulting to 5. Writes `prio

`, `no such task `, or `bad priority

` (a `p` that is not a single digit 0–9 changes nothing). - **`list`**: open tasks are sorted by priority ascending, then id ascending. Line format is unchanged. - **`list all`**: every task, finished ones included, in the same order, prefixed with `-` (open) or `x` (finished). - **Unknown command**: writes `? `. **Choices I made where the brief was silent** - For `prio`, I check that the id exists before checking the priority, so `prio 9 x` on a missing task writes `no such task 9`. - `list` with any argument other than exactly `all` behaves as the plain open list, as it did before. - A line starting with a space has an empty first word, so it writes `? ` with nothing after it. **Verification** - `deno check` passes. - I ran three sample command files covering priority reordering, the bad-id and bad-priority errors, `list all` marks and ordering, unknown commands, and the original commands. The output matched the spec. - The tie-break by id is in the comparator, but my samples never exercised it with two tasks of equal priority in a way that would have failed if it were missing. The directory is not a git repository, so I did not commit. I did not add test files to the directory, since the brief says the contract is the specification.
